**re: Pick a concept — student attendance — and show which standards model it and, for each mapping to CEDS, its relation, confidence and source.** Student attendance is one of the most densely cross-linked concepts in the graph. Here is a full structural breakdown across every standard that models it, organized by the CEDS hub concepts they resolve to. All mappings below are **inferred** (judge: `bridge-jev`) — none are authored; treat them as judgment, not established fact. --- ## How the Standards Model Student Attendance The concept splits across two distinct CEDS anchors: | CEDS Hub Property | CEDS ID | Domain | |---|---|---| | **Number of Days Absent** | P000201 | Role Attendance | | **Has Absent Attendance Category** | P000599 | Role Attendance Event | These capture different levels: **P000201** is a cumulative scalar count; **P000599** is a per-event categorical classifier. The CEDS value codeset for attendance event type also surfaces a `Daily attendance` concept (option value OV000601115531). --- ## Standard-by-Standard Structural Inventory | Standard | Core Attendance Construct | Structural Location | |---|---|---| | **Ed-Fi 5.2** | `StudentSchoolAttendanceEvent`, `StudentSectionAttendanceEvent`, `StudentProgramAttendanceEvent`, `StudentInterventionAttendanceEvent` (four distinct event entities) | Dedicated `StudentAttendance` domain and interchange | | **SIF 4.3** | `StudentDailyAttendance`, `StudentPeriodAttendance`, `AttendanceCodeInfo` objects; fields: `AttendanceValue`, `AttendanceCode`, `AttendanceStatus`, `AttendanceNote`, `DaysAbsent`, `ExcusedAbsences`, `UnexcusedAbsences`, `CountsTowardAttendance` | Per-object fields on `StudentAttendanceSummary` and `StudentAcademicRecord` | | **PESC (6 schemas)** | `AttendanceCountType` complex type with `DaysAbsent` and `DaysPresent` children; grouped under `AcademicSession` in the academic record | Embedded in `CollegeTranscript`, `HighSchoolTranscript`, `LearningRecord`, `TestScoreReport`, `AcademicEPortfolio` | | **CEDS 14** | `Role Attendance` (cumulative counts) and `Role Attendance Event` (per-event) classes; properties `Number of Days Absent`, `Has Absent Attendance Category`, `Student Attendance Rate`, etc. | Hub — is the reference anchor | PESC does not have a standalone attendance schema; attendance is always a subordinate element within an academic record section. --- ## Mappings to CEDS — Full Detail All mappings are **inferred / bridge-jev**.  --- ## Key Findings **1. Ed-Fi is the most event-granular.** It models four distinct attendance event types (school, section, program, intervention), which is richer than any other standard here. Its `AttendanceEventReason` maps **narrow** to CEDS `Has Absent Attendance Category` — Ed-Fi's free-text reason is more specific than CEDS's categorical codeset. **2. SIF is the most terminologically precise for aggregate counts.** Its `DaysAbsent` in `StudentAcademicRecord` lands an **EXACT_MATCH** to CEDS `Number of Days Absent` at confidence 0.9 — the strongest single-element alignment in the attendance cluster. Notably, SIF's `UnexcusedAbsences` and `ExcusedAbsences` both map **BROAD** to the same CEDS property, correctly reflecting that CEDS `Number of Days Absent` is an undifferentiated total while SIF models the sub-types. **3. PESC is architecturally consistent but context-embedded.** All six PESC schemas carry `DaysAbsent` inside `AttendanceCountType`, always nested in an academic session within an academic record. Every instance lands a **CLOSE_MATCH** at 0.9 confidence — strong but not exact, reflecting the session-scoped context vs. CEDS's role-level property. **4. The SIF `ExcusedAbsences` / `UnexcusedAbsences` split exposes a real semantic gap.** CEDS 14 does not publish a separate "excused absence count" property at the same level — the judge correctly calls both BROAD against the combined concept. This is a genuine interoperability wrinkle if you need to distinguish absence types across SIF and a CEDS-aligned system. **5. No PESC or Ed-Fi standard maps to `Has Absent Attendance Category` with EXACT confidence.** The absence-category codeset concept in CEDS (which classifies *why* a student was absent) is only weakly covered by other standards, suggesting a gap worth investigating for compliance use cases.
